landing.title: A quiet place to write, one page a day.
landing.description: myjournal is a personal journal for one plain-text entry per day. Write about today, revisit past entries, browse your calendar, and move entries to trash. Your saved files live in your own Google Drive.
landing.kicker: Private journaling in your own Drive
landing.feature.quiet.title: Quiet by design
landing.feature.quiet.body: One page a day, intentionally simple, with no extra clutter competing with your writing.
landing.feature.drive.title: Stored in your Drive
landing.feature.drive.body: Your journal lives in a plain-text folder in your own Google Drive, not in a proprietary app database.
landing.feature.recovery.title: Easy to recover
landing.feature.recovery.body: Unsaved drafts stay in this browser tab for recovery. Clear save states help you see when your writing still needs attention. An internet connection is required to load and save entries.

help.title: Help
help.description: A practical guide to writing, saving, and managing your journal in Google Drive.
help.howItWorks.title: How it works
help.howItWorks.body: Write one plain-text entry per day. Today opens in your browser’s time zone; past dates remain editable and future dates are unavailable. Use Entries to browse previews or Calendar to choose a date. Entries are stored as UTF-8 text files under myjournal/entries/<year>/YYYY-MM-DD.txt in your Google Drive.
help.access.title: What it can and cannot see
help.access.body: Google sign-in identifies your account. The drive.file permission allows access to files and folders created by myjournal or explicitly made available through that permission; it does not grant access to all of Drive. The app presents its own journal files. You can inspect your saved files directly in Google Drive.
help.reconnect.title: When to reconnect
help.reconnect.body: If Google access expires or is revoked, reconnect when prompted. Keep unsaved text safe before navigating away and reconnect to the same account. Google Testing connections may expire sooner than the app’s maximum 30-day sign-in lifetime. Reconnecting does not recover drafts from a closed tab.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: How myjournal handles your Google account data, journal entries, and browser storage.
privacy.storage: Saved entries are UTF-8 plain-text files in your Google Drive, under myjournal/entries/<year>/YYYY-MM-DD.txt. Requests pass through the myjournal server so it can communicate with Google. The app has no production journal or user database. It temporarily processes entry content in memory and retains bounded in-memory entry content, previews and date indexes for up to two minutes; a process restart clears these caches. Your writing is not end-to-end encrypted by myjournal.
privacy.cookie: Your account connection, including refresh credentials, is held in an encrypted, authenticated HttpOnly cookie with a fixed maximum lifetime of 30 days from sign-in. Google permission can expire or be revoked sooner. A separate encrypted login cookie lasts up to ten minutes. Cookies use Secure on production HTTPS. Unsaved recovery drafts are stored separately for each account, date, and tab in sessionStorage; they may survive reloads and same-tab navigation, but are not an offline sync service. Acknowledged saves, confirmed trash, or successful sign-out remove the relevant drafts. Failed operations can retain drafts for recovery. The app also stores your chosen theme and browser time zone. Your language preference is stored in a separate browser cookie for up to one year and remains after sign-out.

landing.access.title: Your journal, connected to your Drive
landing.access.body: Google sign-in identifies your account. The drive.file permission lets myjournal create and manage the journal files and folders it creates, without access to all the files in your Drive. You can disconnect in Settings and keep your saved files.
privacy.intro: myjournal is a personal journaling app that stores one plain-text entry per day in your Google Drive. This policy describes the production Google-connected app. Local filesystem storage is used only for development.
privacy.data.title: Data we access
privacy.data.body: When you connect Google, myjournal requests openid, email, profile, and https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file. It uses your Google account identifier and email to identify your connection and show the connected account. Google may return basic profile information during sign-in; myjournal does not need your profile photo to provide journaling. OAuth access and refresh tokens allow the app to act on your permission. Drive access covers files and folders created by the app or explicitly made available to it through that permission, rather than your entire Drive.
privacy.use.title: How we use your data
privacy.use.body: myjournal uses your account information and tokens to sign you in, maintain your Google connection, and keep accounts separate. It processes journal text, file identifiers, dates, folder metadata, and content versions to load, save, list, preview, and trash your entries and detect conflicting edits. Data is used to provide these journaling features, not for advertising, profiling, or training AI models.
privacy.storage.title: Where data is stored
privacy.browser.title: Cookies and browser drafts
privacy.sharing.title: Sharing and service providers
privacy.sharing.body: Google provides sign-in and Drive storage. Railway hosts the app and processes requests passing through the service. myjournal does not sell Google user data, share journal content with advertisers, or use tracking or analytics scripts. Data is transferred as needed to provide the service or when required by law. Hosting providers may process network information such as IP addresses under their own policies. Do not include journal content or credentials when contacting support unless you intentionally choose to share them.
privacy.logs.title: Operational logs and security
privacy.logs.body: Application request logs record method, query-free path, response status, duration, and request ID; paths can include entry dates. The app avoids logging journal text, credentials, whole cookies, and OAuth callback query values. Encryption protects the connection cookie, and HTTPS protects production traffic. Platform-level log retention is controlled by the hosting provider; myjournal does not promise a particular platform retention period or absolute security.
privacy.control.title: Retention, disconnect, and deletion
privacy.control.body: Your saved files remain in Google Drive until you remove them. Moving an entry to trash in myjournal uses Drive Trash, not permanent deletion. You can manage or permanently delete files and empty Trash in Google Drive. Settings → Disconnect revokes myjournal’s Google access and signs you out after revocation succeeds; it does not delete saved files. Sign out alone clears the app session without revoking Google access. You can also revoke access in your Google Account. Successful sign-out clears this account’s drafts in the active tab and notifies other open tabs; inspect other tabs or clear site data if cleanup fails. Clear site data to remove remaining browser storage. Support cannot erase files from your Drive after access is revoked.
privacy.limited.title: Google API Limited Use
privacy.limited.body: myjournal’s use and transfer of information received from Google APIs adheres to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.
privacy.limited.link: Google API Services User Data Policy
privacy.contact.title: Contact and policy updates
privacy.contact.body: For privacy questions or help with data deletion, contact
privacy.changes: Changes to these practices will be reflected on this page with an updated date. Review this policy before reconnecting if the requested permissions change.
terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.description: The conditions for using myjournal, a quiet journal in your own Google Drive.
terms.service.title: Using myjournal
terms.service.body: These terms apply when you use myjournal. The app provides one plain-text journal entry per day, with browsing, calendar navigation, and trash controls. You need an internet connection and a Google account with available Drive storage. Access may be limited to approved test users while the app is in testing. If you do not agree to these terms, do not use the service.
terms.writing.title: Your writing
terms.writing.body: You retain ownership of your journal entries. You give myjournal permission to process your entries and account connection only as needed to provide the service, as described in the privacy policy. You are responsible for the content you save and for having the rights to use it. We do not claim ownership of your writing.
terms.conduct.title: Responsible use
terms.conduct.body: Use only accounts you are authorized to access. Do not use the service for unlawful activity, attempt to access another person’s data, bypass access controls, or disrupt the app or its providers. Keep your Google account and the devices you use secure.
terms.availability.title: Availability and keeping your files safe
terms.availability.body: myjournal depends on Google Drive, hosting services, and your connection. Availability, uninterrupted access, and error-free saves are not guaranteed. Keep independent copies of writing that matters to you. Browser drafts are temporary recovery aids, not permanent backups or offline synchronization. Closing a tab or clearing site data can remove them. Google controls Drive storage, Trash, and revision retention.
terms.conflicts.title: Saving and conflicting edits
terms.conflicts.body: The app checks content versions to help detect changes, but Google Drive updates are not an atomic compare-and-save operation. Simultaneous editing in another app, browser tab, or overlapping server deployment can cause lost updates or duplicate entries. Avoid simultaneous editing of the same entry and check save feedback before leaving the page. Keep a copy of unsaved text when an operation fails.
terms.disconnect.title: Ending your connection
terms.disconnect.body: You may stop using myjournal at any time. Sign out removes the app session; Disconnect in Settings also revokes its Google access when revocation succeeds. Saved files remain in your Drive. Moving an entry to trash does not permanently delete it; manage permanent deletion in Google Drive. We may restrict or suspend access to address misuse, security issues, or service changes.
terms.changes.title: Service and terms changes
terms.changes.body: Features and availability may change, and the service may be discontinued. Changes to these terms will appear here with an updated date. Review changes before continuing to use the app. Nothing in these terms excludes rights or obligations that cannot be excluded under applicable law.
terms.contact.title: Privacy and contact
terms.contact.body: Read how myjournal handles account information, journal content, and browser storage in the privacy policy. For questions about these terms, contact
help.saving.title: Saving and recovery
help.saving.body: After an entry loads successfully, changes save after five seconds of idle typing. You can also use Save. Leaving the editor or hiding the page attempts a save, but is not a guarantee. Check for Saved before leaving. Unsaved drafts are backed up separately in this browser tab when browser storage is available. Recovered drafts wait for editing or Save before autosave resumes. Closing the tab or clearing site data can remove the backup.
help.failure.title: If loading or saving fails
help.failure.body: Keep the page open and copy unsaved text somewhere safe. Retry a failed load before editing. A failed save pauses automatic writes; use Save to retry and follow the displayed instructions. If browser backup is unavailable, do not rely on a draft being recoverable after navigation. myjournal requires an internet connection to load and save entries.
help.conflicts.title: Conflicting changes
help.conflicts.body: If an entry changed elsewhere, review the conflict choices. Keep mine reads the latest version and attempts to save your text. Load the other version asks before replacing your draft. Keep both combines the versions for review before Save. Further changes can cause another conflict. Avoid editing the same entry simultaneously in another tab or directly in Drive; conflict checks cannot guarantee protection against every external write.
help.delete.title: Trash, sign out, and Disconnect
help.delete.body: Moving an entry to trash requires confirmation and uses Google Drive Trash. Restore or permanently delete it in Drive. Sign out ends your app session; Disconnect in Settings also revokes Google access. Neither deletes saved files. Save or copy unsaved text first: successful sign-out clears this account’s browser drafts. If cleanup fails after sign-out, use the cleanup retry shown on the page.
help.contact.title: Need more help?
help.contact.body: Contact support without including journal entries, passwords, or sign-in credentials. You can read more about data handling and service conditions below.
